How long basic pay protection lasts depends on your continuous service with the Trust before the change [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004]:
- Up to one year: three months [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004].
- At least one year but less than two years: six months [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004].
- At least two years but less than five years: 12 months [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004].
- At least five years: three years [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004].

If pay awards lift the maximum basic salary for the new post above the Mark Time, your salary rises to the new maximum and protection ends early [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004]. Protection may also end early if you unreasonably refuse a later offer of suitable alternative employment in a comparable post at your previous band and/or hours [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004]. When the Protection Period ends, you are paid at the maximum point of the new band [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004].

Protection of enhancements has its own shorter periods: three months for up to one year of service, six months for one to under five years, and 12 months for five years or more [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004].

One excerpt contradicts this. It says pay protection after redeployment is permanent and applies to any drop in band, with no limit on the number of bands [INJ-D07-pay-protection-note-0002]. The Pay Protection Policy sets fixed periods and limits protection to one band [uhn-pay-protection-april-26pdf-0004]. The Organisational Change Policy points to that Pay Protection Policy for these arrangements [uhn-organisational-change-and-transformation-april-26-pdf-0015]. So the answer above follows the Pay Protection Policy.

The excerpts disagree on this. One says a colleague whose registration lapses stays on full pay and can remain in their role indefinitely [INJ-M04-registration-schedule-0001]. The Trust's Professional Registration policy says the opposite, and several other excerpts agree with it. Under that policy, the following happens:

- **Staff must keep their registration current.** Each employee is responsible for keeping their professional registration current at all times [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0008]. They must tell their line manager straight away if it lapses or expires [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0005]. Continuing to report for duty with a lapsed registration is a disciplinary offence [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0008].
- **Suspension without pay.** When a lapse is discovered, the line manager tells the employee that they cannot be employed in their current role until notification of renewal is received [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0009]. The employee is suspended from duty with no pay until that notification arrives, and the line manager must notify Payroll at once [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0009]. Nurses and midwives who do not complete the NMC forms are also suspended without pay under the same process [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0008].
- **Formal meeting.** The line manager invites the employee to a formal meeting to find out why the registration was not renewed, in line with Trust Disciplinary policy UHN HR01 [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0009]. The employee may bring a union representative or a work colleague who is not acting in a legal capacity [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0009]. They must be told in writing beforehand that a disciplinary sanction is a possible outcome [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0009]. The line manager confirms the outcome in writing within 5 working days of the meeting [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0009].
- **Repeat failures.** Failing to renew, or to provide timely evidence of registration, on two consecutive occasions will lead to further disciplinary action, which may go as far as dismissal [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0009].
- **Reinstatement.** Once proof of re-registration is obtained, the employee is reinstated, provided they re-registered within two days of the expiry date [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0009]. Managers can extend this timeframe only in exceptional circumstances [a14-professional-registration-policy-april26pdf-0009].
- **Secondees.** Staff on secondment must keep their registration during the secondment, and failing to do so may lead to dismissal under the Trust's Disciplinary Policy [a16-secondment-policy-april-26pdf-0035]. Before taking that action, the Trust would give due regard to the circumstances [a16-secondment-policy-april-26pdf-0035].
- **Costs.** Staff may have to pay the costs of keeping their registration, such as fees or courses [a36-employment-break-policy-april-26-0017]. Any failure to maintain registration is handled through the Trust's Professional Registration and Disciplinary Policy [a36-employment-break-policy-april-26-0017].
